## Overview

Apples provide **pectin**, **quercetin** and **vitamin C** in an intact fruit structure. Whole fruit is more filling and produces a smaller post-meal insulin response than apple juice [1].

Within the BRAIN Diet, apples are best eaten as whole fruit rather than juice. Leave the skin on when tolerated; much of the flavonol content is in the peel [3].

## Key Nutritional Highlights

- Whole fruit is more filling and blunts the post-meal insulin response compared with juice [1].
- **Pectin** is present; USDA reports total fibre and does not quantify pectin [5].
- **Quercetin** and related flavonols are concentrated in the peel [3].
- Best eaten as whole fruit with the skin when tolerated.

## Food Context

### Preparation

- Prefer whole fresh apples to preserve food-matrix benefits and blunt glycemic response [1].
- Avoid juicing or heavy processing that removes fibre and disrupts cell-wall structure [1].
- Leave skin on when tolerated; much of the flavonol content concentrates in peel tissue [3].

[3] Neveu & Perez-Jimenez (2010). [Phenol-Explorer: an online comprehensive database on polyphenol contents in foods](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#neveu_phenol-explorer_2010). Phenol-Explorer reports quercetin and related flavonols in apples, with higher values in peel than in flesh.

[5] Liu et al. (2023). [A wide diversity exists in pectin structure from thirteen apple cultivars](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#liu_apple_pectin_2023). Isolated pectin from 13 apple cultivars as alcohol-insoluble, water-soluble and chelating-soluble fractions; yields varied by cultivar and are not a USDA per-100 g pectin quantity, nor the 2.4 g total fibre on this page.

## Overview

Broccoli is a cruciferous vegetable providing **glucoraphanin**, the precursor of [sulforaphane](/docs/substances/bioactive-compounds/organosulfur/sulforaphane), together with **folate** and **vitamin C** at low energy density. Sulforaphane forms when myrosinase meets that precursor. Heating can stop the enzyme while glucoraphanin remains [1,4].

The nutrient table does not give a sulforaphane amount per 100 g. In one UK lot, sous-vide cooking at 100 °C for 20 minutes left 1.06 µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight. The same cooked broccoli plus 1 g brown mustard powder formed 8.58 µmol/g dry weight. Twelve adults who ate 200 g excreted 9.8 µmol of the urinary metabolite per g creatinine in 24 hours, and 44.7 µmol/g creatinine when the mustard was added [4].

## Food Context

### Synergies

- Include broccoli with a varied meal rather than treating it as a sulforaphane dose.

### Preparation

- Chopping or chewing lets broccoli myrosinase meet glucoraphanin and form sulforaphane [1].
- In the Okunade sous-vide series at 100 °C, myrosinase activity fell by 40% after 2 minutes and by 90% after 6 minutes. None was measurable after 8 minutes. The feeding meal was cooked for 20 minutes [4].
- After that long cook, urinary sulforaphane-NAC was still detected. The authors read that remainder as conversion by gut microbes, and it varied between the 12 adults [4].
- Adding 1 g brown mustard powder after cooking supplied active myrosinase. In the florets, 8.58 / 1.06 = 8.1, reported as an 8-fold rise. In urine, 44.7 / 9.8 = 4.6 from the published means. The average of each person's increase was 4.7-fold, from 1.7-fold to 10-fold [4].
